---
title: "VideoAnnotator results in R"
output: html_document
---

This notebook reads VideoAnnotator's **results table**: every pipeline's results in one CSV, one
row per event and measure, the same columns for every pipeline. It walks through a small analysis
of the demo clip (a parent and infant playing peekaboo) that ships beside this notebook.

**To use your own results**, export the table (the viewer's *Export → Table (CSV)* on a run or job
page, or `videoannotator export table <results folder>`) and change `TABLE` below. Everything else
runs unchanged; sections whose pipeline you didn't run say so and move on.

Packages: `readr`, `dplyr`, `tidyr`, `ggplot2` (all in the tidyverse). The columns are documented
in `docs/usage/exporting_results.md`.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
TABLE <- "demo_clip_table.csv"

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Read every column with the type the table's contract gives it.
results <- read_csv(
  TABLE,
  col_types = cols(
    run = col_character(), video = col_character(), pipeline = col_character(),
    event = col_integer(), track = col_character(), start = col_double(),
    end = col_double(), frame = col_integer(), measure = col_character(),
    label = col_character(), value = col_double(), confidence = col_double(),
    x = col_double(), y = col_double(), width = col_double(), height = col_double(),
    model = col_character(), videoannotator_version = col_character(),
    file = col_character()
  )
)
cat(nrow(results), "rows,", n_distinct(results$video), "video(s),",
    n_distinct(results$pipeline), "pipelines\n")
```

## What's in the table

Each row is one **measure** of one **event**. An event is something a pipeline found: a person in
a frame, a face, a speech segment, a speaker turn, a scene, a VLM label. Its first row says what it
is (`person`, `face`, `speech`…); further rows with the same `event` number are things measured
about it (an emotion, an action-unit intensity, gaze). `start` and `end` are seconds from the start
of the video; `end` is empty (`NA`) for something seen at one moment (a frame).

```{r overview}
results |> count(pipeline, measure, name = "rows")
```

## Who speaks, and for how long

Speaker turns come from diarization (`speaker_turn` rows; `track` is the speaker). Speaker labels
are anonymous (`SPEAKER_00`, …): diarization tells voices apart, it doesn't know who they are.

```{r speaking-time}
turns <- results |> filter(measure == "speaker_turn") |> mutate(duration = end - start)
if (nrow(turns) == 0) {
  cat("No speaker diarization in this table.\n")
} else {
  turns |> group_by(video, track) |> summarise(turns = n(), seconds = sum(duration), .groups = "drop")
}
```

## What was said

Speech recognition gives one `speech` row per segment, with the text in `label`.

```{r speech}
results |> filter(measure == "speech") |> select(video, start, end, label)
```

## Who is in view, when

Person tracking gives one `person` row per detection, with a `track` that follows the same person
across frames and a `label` (`parent`, `infant`, …). The labels come from a size heuristic, so check
them: in the demo clip both detected people are labelled `parent`.

```{r people}
people <- results |> filter(measure == "person")
if (nrow(people) == 0) {
  cat("No person tracking in this table.\n")
} else {
  print(people |> group_by(track, label) |>
          summarise(detections = n(), first = min(start), last = max(start), .groups = "drop"))
  ggplot(people, aes(x = start, y = track)) +
    geom_point(shape = "|", size = 6) +
    labs(x = "seconds", y = NULL, title = "Detections per tracked person")
}
```

## Facial expression over time

Face pipelines measure several things per face. `emotion` rows hold the most likely expression in
`label` with its probability in `confidence`; `emotion_score` rows hold every expression's score
(`label` names it, `value` is the score). OpenFace adds `action_unit` rows (one per action unit).

```{r expression}
results |> filter(measure == "emotion") |> count(pipeline, label, name = "faces")

units <- results |> filter(measure == "action_unit")
if (nrow(units) > 0) {
  units |>
    group_by(label, start) |>
    summarise(intensity = mean(value), .groups = "drop") |>
    ggplot(aes(x = start, y = intensity, colour = label)) +
    geom_line() + geom_point(size = 0.8) +
    labs(x = "seconds", y = "intensity (mean over faces)", colour = NULL,
         title = "OpenFace action units")
}
```

## One row per event: going wide

The long layout keeps every pipeline in the same columns. For per-face analysis you often want one
row per face with a column per action unit: that's one `pivot_wider` call.

```{r wide}
if (nrow(units) == 0) {
  cat("No OpenFace results in this table.\n")
} else {
  units |>
    select(video, pipeline, event, start, label, value) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = label, values_from = value)
}
```

## Who is in view while someone speaks

Combining pipelines is a join on time. For each speaker turn, which tracked people were detected
during it? People are sampled at moments, so a person counts as in view during a turn if any of
their detections falls inside it.

```{r overlap}
if (nrow(turns) == 0 || nrow(people) == 0) {
  cat("Needs both speaker diarization and person tracking.\n")
} else {
  turns |>
    select(video, speaker = track, turn_start = start, turn_end = end) |>
    left_join(people |> select(video, person = track, seen_at = start),
              by = "video", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
    filter(is.na(seen_at) | (seen_at >= turn_start & seen_at <= turn_end)) |>
    group_by(video, speaker, turn_start, turn_end) |>
    summarise(people_in_view = paste(sort(unique(na.omit(person))), collapse = ", "),
              .groups = "drop") |>
    right_join(turns |> select(video, speaker = track, turn_start = start, turn_end = end),
               by = c("video", "speaker", "turn_start", "turn_end")) |>
    mutate(people_in_view = coalesce(na_if(people_in_view, ""), "(none detected)")) |>
    arrange(video, turn_start)
}
```

## What made these results

Every row names the models (`model`) and VideoAnnotator version that produced it; `not recorded`
means the file came from a version that didn't record it. For a citable methods paragraph with
exact weight revisions, use *Export → Methods paragraph* or `videoannotator export methods`.

```{r provenance}
results |> count(pipeline, model, videoannotator_version, name = "rows")
```
